Network diagnostics confirmed that the application could successfully reach the `peer` service when the environment variable `PEER_HOST` was set to `peer`. A previous configuration set `PEER_HOST` to `peer.prod`.

The smallest justified change to restore health was to revert the `PEER_HOST` environment variable in the application deployment to `peer` and to slightly increase the `initialDelaySeconds` on the readiness probe to allow the application enough time to initialize its readiness loop.

**Applied Changes:**
1.  Patched Deployment `app` to set `readinessProbe.initialDelaySeconds` to `5`.
2.  Patched Deployment `app` to set container environment variable `PEER_HOST` to `peer`.

**Observed Outcome:**
The rolling update successfully replaced the faulty pods. A fresh observation confirms both application pods are now healthy and ready:
`kubectl get pods -n default -l app=app` returned:
```
NAME                   READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
app-6db94577bf-tkx8x   1/1     Running   0          40s
app-6db94577bf-twmkp   1/1     Running   0          40s
```
The application is now in a healthy state, and the readiness probe confirms successful peer communication.

I will report the change and the verified outcome.
